cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, is guiding God's people through the wilderness after leaving Egypt. Now they set out from Mount Hor along the route to the Red Sea. It's the long way around, friend.

cards.question: Why does Israel take the long way toward the Red Sea?

answers.text: To go around the land of Edom

cards.text: Going around Edom means more road, more walking, more days. Let's see how the people handle that.

cards.question: How do the people handle the long journey around Edom?

answers.text: They stop to rest for weeks

cards.text: Impatient. You know when the GPS adds forty minutes and somebody in the back seat sighs real LOUD? Now picture a whole nation in that back seat, and they don't keep it to themselves.

cards.question: The impatient people start speaking out. Who do they speak against?
The people ask why they were led out of Egypt to die in the wilderness. What do they say there is none of?

cards.text: Then they say, "we detest this wretched food!" Friend, after years of nothing but drawer dust, I'd have said THANK YOU for one single crumb.

cards.question: After the people speak against Him, what does the LORD send among them?
Only a few of the Israelites are bitten by the venomous snakes.

cards.text: Snakes in the camp, and people bitten and dying. Then the same people who spoke against Moses come walking right up to him.

cards.question: The people tell Moses, "We have ___ by speaking against the LORD and against you."
What do the bitten people ask Moses to do for them?

answers.text: Intercede so the LORD takes the snakes away
Lead them back down to Egypt
Build a wall around the camp

cards.text: So Moses interceded for the people, the very ones who just spoke against him. Friend, if a whole crowd spoke against ME, I'd need three batches and a LONG nap before I prayed for anybody.

cards.question: After Moses intercedes, what does the LORD tell him to make?

answers.text: A fiery serpent on a pole

cards.text: A fiery serpent, mounted on a pole. That's the whole instruction sheet, friend.

cards.question: The LORD tells Moses who will live once the serpent is on the pole. Who is it?

answers.text: Anyone bitten who looks at it
Anyone bitten who touches the pole
Anyone bitten who offers a lamb

cards.question: Moses gets to work on the snake for the pole. What does he make it out of?
Only the first bitten person to look at the bronze snake would live.

cards.text: If anyone who was bitten looked at the bronze snake, he would live. One look, friend. I've waited LONGER than that for an oven to preheat.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 12 quotes "We have ___ by speaking against the LORD and against you.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The stop has 9 multiple choice cards, 2 true or false cards and 1 fill in the blank card. Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The card mostly restates card 2's answer (going around Edom means more road) and tells nothing new from the passage before card 4.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: "Impatient.", the GPS sentence and the "Now picture" sentence. Story cards other than the opening card must be 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke sets Papa Dorin above the people ("I'd have said THANK YOU for one single crumb") and laughs at their complaint instead of at himself or with their situation.

rule.text: Humble. When a joke needs someone to laugh at, it's himself. Humor about people in Bible stories laughs with their human situation, never at them.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "waited" makes the line nonsense ("We have waited by speaking against the LORD"). It isn't believable and it doesn't match the other answers in kind.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The question calls them "the bitten people." Numbers 21:7 says only "the people" came to Moses. The text doesn't say they were all bitten.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The joke has Papa Dorin needing three batches and a long nap before he would pray for people who spoke against him. That makes him slow to forgive, which goes against his character.

rule.text: Godly character. He never holds a grudge, and his humor reflects kindness and forgiveness.

findings.problem: The card only restates card 15's answer. It also calls that the whole instruction, but in Numbers 21:8 the LORD goes on to say that anyone bitten who looks at it will live.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The story card recaps the answer just given on card 15 and doesn't move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: the verse retelling, "One look, friend." and the oven line.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card restates what cards 17 and 19 already established (anyone bitten who looks will live) and adds nothing new from the passage.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.
